news.headline: Analyst consensus remains Buy heading into Aug 3 earnings, with a median 12-month target near $200 (~61% above the current price) across 35 analysts
news.why_it_matters: Sell-side confidence is intact ahead of the print despite the stock trading 40% off its all-time high amid a broader enterprise-software selloff, supporting the long-term thesis for a multi-year holder.

news.headline: Valuation remains stretched at roughly 130-150x trailing earnings and ~60x price/sales
news.why_it_matters: A premium this large raises the stakes for the Aug 3 print - any guidance miss or growth deceleration could trigger an outsized re-rating even for a long-term holder.

news.headline: Q2 results beat expectations (EPS $0.12 vs $0.11 est., revenue ~$1.2B) with member count up 35% and products up 42%, and full-year guidance was raised
news.why_it_matters: Confirms the 'everything app' growth thesis (lending strength, record originations, member growth) remains intact, which is the core reason for a multi-year hold.

news.headline: Shares are recovering today after an initial post-earnings selloff driven by unchanged near-term profit guidance and rising growth spend; Truist nudged its target to $18 but kept a Hold
news.why_it_matters: The market is still debating whether higher growth investment delays profitability - worth watching over the next few quarters, though today's rebound suggests dip-buyers see it as reinvestment rather than a fundamental problem.

news.headline: NYSE notified Surf Air Mobility on July 24 that shares no longer meet the $1.00 minimum average closing price requirement over a 30-day period; the company has a 6-month cure window
news.why_it_matters: Real delisting risk for a multi-year holder, though a board-approved reverse-split backstop is already in place and the stock continues trading normally during the cure period.

news.headline: APLD rebounded ~20% today, riding Microsoft's blowout cloud earnings and a broader AI-infrastructure sector rally rather than APLD-specific news
news.why_it_matters: A sector-wide re-rating that nonetheless supports the multi-year hyperscaler-demand thesis underpinning APLD's leased-capacity model.

news.headline: Wednesday's post-earnings drop (-12.8%) reflected the market digging into the composition of this week's revenue beat: $152.4M came from one-time, low-margin tenant fit-out fees rather than recurring hosting revenue, alongside a ~$5B debt load and a $249.2M full-year GAAP net loss
news.why_it_matters: The core overhang for a long-term holder - heavy leverage funding the buildout raises financing/dilution risk if capital markets tighten, even as the long-term contracted-revenue growth story remains positive.

news.headline: No SERV-specific catalyst found today; the ~9.8% bounce tracks a broad Nasdaq/AI-infrastructure rebound (Microsoft's cloud beat lifting the whole sector) ahead of the confirmed Aug 6 earnings date
news.why_it_matters: Today's move is macro/sector beta, not a change to the business thesis - focus stays on the Aug 6 print for a deeply oversold, cash-burning position.

news.headline: NOW fell again today (-4.9%) even after this week's strong Q2 beat (revenue +24% YoY, guidance raised), as SaaS/application-layer names broadly underperformed amid rotation into AI-infrastructure winners like Microsoft
news.why_it_matters: Looks like sector rotation/profit-taking rather than new company-specific bad news, giving back part of the post-earnings rally without a change in fundamentals.

news.headline: At least one sell-side analyst argues the pullback is overdone, seeing up to 115% upside from current levels on AI-platform momentum even though NOW is down nearly 50% over the past year
news.why_it_matters: A bullish counter-read worth tracking, though it also underscores how much value the stock has lost over the trailing year despite billion-dollar AI platform milestones.

news.headline: MSFT jumped as much as 17% intraday - the largest single-day market-cap gain in stock market history - after Q4 results showed Azure growth accelerating to 43% and Azure revenue crossing $100B for the first time; Copilot seats topped 30 million
news.why_it_matters: Confirms the AI/cloud re-rating is durable rather than a one-day pop, reinforcing the long-term thesis, though a move this sharp raises near-term profit-taking risk.

news.headline: Analysts maintain Buy ratings with an average price target near $560 (~24% above today's close); FY2027 capex guidance was raised to $255-260B to fund the AI buildout
news.why_it_matters: Sell-side confidence that AI capex is translating into Azure revenue is the key debate for a multi-year holder; the higher capex is a 1-3 year margin variable to monitor even though the market is currently rewarding it.

news.headline: ORCL rallied ~8% after announcing an expanded partnership bringing Google's Gemini 3.1/3.5 models into Oracle Fusion Applications, NetSuite, and AI Agent Studio
news.why_it_matters: Diversifies Oracle's AI-model ecosystem beyond OpenAI (now including Google alongside Meta, xAI, Cohere, Alibaba), directly countering the OpenAI-concentration/credit-risk narrative behind the recent S&P downgrade.

news.headline: Microsoft's blowout Azure results sparked a sector-wide cloud/AI rally today
news.why_it_matters: Confirms enterprise cloud demand remains robust and easing fears of an AI capex bubble - a supportive read-through for Oracle's own OCI backlog.

news.headline: Zillow's own research shows starter-home sales falling 5.4% YoY even as starter inventory rises, while luxury-home sales strengthen - a bifurcated housing market
news.why_it_matters: A proprietary data point suggesting softer transaction volume at the entry-level tier Zillow's marketplace depends most on for lead generation.

news.headline: Shares pared an earlier intraday decline to close down modestly, as another securities-fraud class action tied to the Redfin rental-listing-agreement allegations was filed ahead of the Aug 10 lead-plaintiff deadline
news.why_it_matters: Largely duplicative litigation on an already-known case, but the accumulation of filings keeps legal overhang elevated heading into Aug 5 earnings and the Aug 24 FTC antitrust trial start.
